'''Yasmin Fahimi''' (born 25 December 1967) is a German trade unionist and politician who has been chairing the [[German Trade Union Confederation]] (DGB) since 2022.<ref>Frank Specht (9 May 2022), [https://www.handelsblatt.com/politik/deutschland/gewerkschaften-mit-93-2-prozent-gewaehlt-yasmin-fahimi-ist-die-erste-frau-an-der-dgb-spitze/28316994.html Mit 93,2 Prozent gewählt – Yasmin Fahimi ist die erste Frau an der DGB-Spitze] ''[[Handelsblatt]]''.</ref>

From 2017 to 2022, Fahimi served as a member of the German [[Bundestag]]. From January 2014 to December 2015 she was the general secretary of the [[Social Democratic Party of Germany|Social Democratic Party]] (SPD).<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/world/europe/no-easy-answer-for-merkel-on-eu-job-1.1818089 |title=No easy answer for Merkel on EU job |newspaper=The Irish Times |author=Scally, Derek |date=3 June 2014 |access-date=27 September 2014}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Anger Mounts as Germany Unearths Second U.S. Spy Suspect |work=Newsweek |agency=Reuters |date=9 July 2014 |url=https://www.newsweek.com/anger-mounts-germany-unearths-second-us-spy-suspect-258057 |access-date=27 September 2014}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Fahimi was born in [[Hanover]]. Her [[Iran]]ian father died in a traffic collision before she was born;<ref>Cordula Eubel (8 November 2016), [https://www.tagesspiegel.de/politik/das-comeback-der-yasmin-fahimi-5234269.html Von der Generalsekretärin zur Staatssekretärin: Das Comeback der Yasmin Fahimi] ''[[Der Tagesspiegel]]''.</ref> her mother is German. Her mother's family comes from East Prussia and fled during World War II. Fahimi has one older brother who was born in Tehran. Fahimi's mother, who was employed at the Ministry of Justice, raised the children alone.

Fahimi studied [[chemistry]] at the [[University of Hanover]] from 1989 to 1998.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Yasmin Fahimi - Munzinger Biographie|url=https://www.munzinger.de/search/go/document.jsp?id=00000029867|access-date=2022-01-26|website=www.munzinger.de}}</ref>

==Early career==
Between 1998 and 2014, Fahimi worked in various capacities at the [[IG Bergbau, Chemie, Energie]]. From 2012, she also served as founder and board member of the Innovationsforum Energiewende, a group convening unions and companies from the energy sector and energy-intensive industries.

==Political career==
Fahimi has been a member of the Social Democratic Party since 1986.<ref>Cordula Eubel (8 November 2016), [https://www.tagesspiegel.de/politik/das-comeback-der-yasmin-fahimi-5234269.html Von der Generalsekretärin zur Staatssekretärin: Das Comeback der Yasmin Fahimi] ''[[Der Tagesspiegel]]''.</ref> She was a member of the federal executive board of the party's [[Young Socialists in the SPD|youth organization]] and from 2009 to 2013 deputy chairwoman of the SPD in Hannover.

In a special party conference on 26 January 2014 Fahimi was elected with 88.5% of the votes to be Secretary General of the SPD under party chairman [[Sigmar Gabriel]], and therefore successor of [[Andrea Nahles]]. By late 2015, Gabriel replaced her with [[Katarina Barley]].

From 2016 until 2018, Fahimi served as State Secretary at the [[Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs]] under the leadership of minister [[Andrea Nahles]].<ref>Cordula Eubel (8 November 2016), [https://www.tagesspiegel.de/politik/das-comeback-der-yasmin-fahimi-5234269.html Von der Generalsekretärin zur Staatssekretärin: Das Comeback der Yasmin Fahimi] ''[[Der Tagesspiegel]]''.</ref> In this capacity, she oversaw the ministry's activities on [[occupational safety and health]]; [[Pensions in Germany|pensions]]; matters concerning people with disabilities; and international employment and social policy (including relations with the [[International Labour Organization]]).

===Member of the German Parliament (2017–2022)===
In November 2016, Fahimi announced that she would run for a parliamentary seat in the [[2017 German federal election|2017 national elections]].<ref>[https://www.bild.de/regional/hannover/yasmin-fahimi/fordert-ursula-von-der-leyen-bei-der-bundestagswahl-heraus-48787920.bild.html Fahimi fordert Ministerin von der Leyen heraus] ''[[Bild]]'', 16 November 2016.</ref>

In parliament, Fahimi served on the Committee on Education, Research and Technology Assessment. As deputy member of the Committee on Foreign Affairs, she was her parliamentary group's [[rapporteur]] on relations to [[Latin America]], the [[Caribbean]], [[Spain]], [[Portugal]], [[Italy]] and [[Malta]]. In addition to her committee assignments, she chaired the German-Brazilian Parliamentary Friendship Group from 2018. Within the SPD parliamentary group, she belonged to the Parliamentary Left, a left-wing movement.<ref>[http://www.parlamentarische-linke.de/unsere-mitglieder/ Members] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150311122743/http://www.parlamentarische-linke.de/unsere-mitglieder/ |date=11 March 2015 }} Parlamentarische Linke.</ref>

In the negotiations to form a so-called [[traffic light coalition]] of the SPD, the [[Alliance 90/The Greens|Green Party]] and the [[Free Democratic Party (Germany)|Free Democratic Party]] (FDP) following the [[2021 German federal election|2021 federal elections]], Fahimi was part of her party's delegation in the working group on labor policy, co-chaired by [[Hubertus Heil]], [[Katharina Dröge]] and [[Johannes Vogel (politician)|Johannes Vogel]].<ref>[https://www.deutschlandfunk.de/ampel-koalition-das-sind-die-verhandlungsteams-von-spd.1939.de.html Ampel-Koalition: Das sind die Verhandlungsteams von SPD, Grünen und FDP]{{Dead link|date=June 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ''[[Deutschlandfunk]]'', October 27, 2021.</ref>

==Chair of DGB (2022–present)==
In 2021 [[German Trade Union Confederation]] (DGB) was looking for a woman to chair the organization. Fahimi's partner, [[Michael Vassiliadis]], head of [[IG Bergbau, Chemie, Energie]], made himself available for the office but was eventually opposed by [[ver.di]], one of the main unions in DGB. Finally, Fahimi met with great approval among all trade unions. She was nominated in January 2022 as new chair of DGB.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Hagelüken|first1=Alexander|last2=Peters|first2=Benedikt|title=DGB: Yasmin Fahimi wird die neue Chefin|url=https://www.sueddeutsche.de/politik/gewerkschaften-dgb-1.5515468|access-date=2022-01-26|website=Süddeutsche.de|date=26 January 2022 |language=de}}</ref>

* [[Bayer]], Member of the supervisory board (since 2022)<ref>[https://www.bayer.com/en/supervisory-board/yasmin-fahimi Supervisory Board: Yasmin Fahimi] [[Bayer]].</ref>

* Hans Böckler Foundation, chair of the Board (since 2022)<ref>[https://www.boeckler.de/de/pressemitteilungen-2675-yasmin-fahimi-steht-dem-vorstand-der-hans-bockler-stiftung-vor-41723.htm Yasmin Fahimi steht dem Vorstand der Hans-Böckler-Stiftung vor] Hans Böckler Foundation, press release of 3 June 2022.</ref>

* Deutsche Industrieforschungsgemeinschaft Konrad Zuse, Member of the Senate<ref>[https://www.zuse-gemeinschaft.de/ueber-uns/struktur/senat Senate] Deutsche Industrieforschungsgemeinschaft Konrad Zuse.</ref>
